bodies.notes: RENAME AND REORGANISATION (all effective 1-2 May 2025). Name: S.I. 180/2025 (in operation 2 May 2025) alters the name from Department of Children, Equality, Disability, Integration and Youth to Department of Children, Disability and Equality, and the Minister's title likewise: https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/pdf/2025/en.si.2025.0180.pdf . Functions OUT to Department of Justice: S.I. 159/2025, Integration and Reception (Transfer of Departmental Administration and Ministerial Functions) Order 2025, in operation 1 May 2025: international protection accommodation (IPAS) and procurement, State-owned centres for international protection, anti-racism policy and migrant integration and its funds, resettlement/temporary protection permissions, plus s.10(2)(l) of the IHREC Act 2014 insofar as it relates to promotion of integration of migrants, and Part 2 of the Civil Law (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2022: https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/pdf/2025/en.si.2025.0159.pdf . Functions OUT to Department of Education: S.I. 181/2025, Youth (Transfer of Departmental Administration and Ministerial Functions) Order 2025, in operation 1 May 2025: functions under the Youth Work Act 2001; s.2(1)(d) and (2) of the Community, Rural and Gaeltacht Affairs (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2007 in so far as they relate to the Young People's Facilities and Services Fund; s.10(1)(j) of the Education and Training Boards Act 2013; and funding, oversight and support of youth work organisations, youth organisations and ETB youth work functions, and youth policy: https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/pdf/2025/en.si.2025.0181.pdf . One small function back IN from Education: S.I. 185/2025 (1 May 2025) transfers the functions under s.18(4)(d) of the Youth Work Act 2001 to the children's department: https://www.irishstatutebook.ie/pdf/2025/en.si.2025.0185.pdf . Earlier (2020, not 2025): youth justice in the community went to the Department of Justice and Oberstown stayed (see iyjs). The three 2025 transfer orders themselves still use the old department name. Education side: Gaisce's 2025 annual report and Tusla's 2025 financial statements both name a 'Department of Education and Youth'; I did not read the order that renamed it. The Youth Participation page (last updated 10 March 2026) still shows the children's department running Comhairle na nÓg after the youth transfer. WHAT WAS READ: gov.ie blocks automated fetching (HTTP 403/405 and a bot-verification page, which I did not attempt to pass), so the department's own pages were read through Internet Archive snapshots of gov.ie (snapshot 5 Oct 2026; aegis page snapshot 16 Apr 2026); the three S.I.s from irishstatutebook.ie directly. The department's 'Functions and Services Provided to the Public' page is dated 2019 and still speaks of the Department of Children and Youth Affairs, so it was not used. Its 'Who Does What' page returned 403 even via the archive. Verdict part, not core: the stated mission sets children alongside disabled people and equality (see openQuestions).

openQuestions.q: Department of Children, Disability and Equality is recorded 'part' because its own mission and Statement of Strategy put children alongside disabled people and equality (and the 2025 transfers took youth and integration out). Should it be core?

Office of the Director of Authorised Intervention, Tuam is recorded 'none': the Act and orders speak of human remains in institutions for 'adults or children, or both', not children; but the site is a former mother and baby institution and the sponsor is the children's department. Include as part/core on a judgement, or leave it out? Also unresolved: the Office was set up for 30 months from 20 March 2023; whether it was extended or closed in 2025 was not established.

Gaisce: core on a 14-25 programme (so partly adults), and its sponsor appears to have moved to the Department of Education and Youth (its own 2025 annual report), while the gov.ie aegis page (May 2025) still says the children's department is the primary funder. Which sponsor should the map show?

Irish Youth Justice Service: no page I read says in terms that it is a unit of the Department of Justice (it is on Justice's policy page, last updated April 2024, with a Justice contact address). Is that enough to place it there?
Tusla Section 56: the 2025 financial statements publish a named recipient list (Appendix 5; 473 s.56 organisations plus 124 SCP). A later stage must decide whether to extract it.

Source route: gov.ie blocks automated fetching, so the department, aegis, strategy, youth-participation, Tuam and Justice youth-justice pages were read via Internet Archive snapshots (URLs show the snapshot). Acceptable as the body's own documents?

Department of Education and Youth is the sponsor of Gaisce and a co-funder of Tusla; the order renaming the Education department was not read. The Department of Education batch should confirm its current name and remit.

health-pss-organisations: these 28 are voluntary organisations (charities/CLGs) that the CSO classifies into central government because of high, conditional government funding. Do you want them kept in the government stage as a grouped "Other" entry, or moved to the voluntary stage (where each would be a profile in its own right and their HSE/DCEDIY grants would be the funding line)? Keeping both would double-count their funding.

health-pss-organisations: in the CSO table these sit under the Department of Children, Disability and Equality (formerly DCEDIY), not the Department of Health, and the universe file records the sponsor only as "Organisations providing health and personal social services". Should the grouped entry be attributed to DCEDIY in the chain? Also, 23 of the 28 were not checked (by instruction); several are not obviously children's services.

department-of-health: gov.ie blocked every page behind human verification (not attempted), so the verdict rests on the Statement of Strategy 2025-2028 and Annual Report 2025 PDFs only. If you can open https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-health/organisation-information/about-the-department-of-health/ and paste the remit text, the function list could be made firmer.

iph: unverified. instituteofpublichealth.org is behind a bot check. Can you open its About page (or an annual report) and tell me whether children are a stated focus? Search results suggested it is an all-island body that may now be named All Island Institute of Public Health.

hiqa: its children's function is inspection of children's social care (Tusla, foster care, special care, Oberstown), not health services. Should that be counted in the health chain or with the children/justice stage? The same question applies to whether inspecting Tusla counts as a "children's service" function of a health regulator.

chi / nphdb: the Children's Health Ireland row has four hospital-level rows in the universe (Connolly, Crumlin, Tallaght, Temple Street), and CHI and NPHDB both relate to the same National Children's Hospital programme. Treat the four hospital rows as part of CHI, and keep NPHDB (capital build) separate from CHI (service) when amounts are added later, to avoid double counting?

hse: Section 38/39 per-agency amounts exist only in Annual Report 2023 Appendix 1 (agencies with grants of 100,000 or more, not labelled Section 38 or 39 in the table as extracted). Is that the right source for the later money stage, and is 2023 the year you want (a 2024 report was not looked for)?

mhc: its remit covers children's mental health services and it is consulting on draft CAMHS standards, but its inspection duty is for approved (inpatient) centres. Is "part / regulates, inspects" the right call, or should CAMHS standards be held back until the Commission's CAMHS role is confirmed in statute?

Name changes affecting later matching: Cope Foundation now trades as Horizons, Brothers of Charity Services Ireland as Corlann, and The Children's Sunshine Home as LauraLynn. The universe still uses the old names.

Teaching Council: coded part/via schools on the strength of 'for the benefit of pupils and students' and its vetting role. The NI equivalent (GTCNI) was coded none. Same treatment for both, or keep Ireland as part?
NCCA and SEC: coded part (NCCA via null because its remit includes early childhood education; SEC via schools). NI's CCEA was part/schools. Is NCCA's early-childhood reach enough to leave via null?

CICA and RIRB (historical abuse): per your NI ruling I was to include them only if there are corresponding voluntary-sector organisations. I cannot assess that from this batch (no voluntary-sector universe was in the brief), so both are recorded normally as part with HISTORICAL scope; decide whether to keep them in the Ireland children's-sector list. CICA's roles are empty because none of the nine role words fits an inquiry: add 'investigates', or leave blank?
CICA: the Department page describing it is 'Last updated on 1 September 2022' and CICA's own site is down (HTTP 500). Is it still a live body? Not established.

Department of Education and Youth: youth work/UBU sits there; early learning and childcare and school-age childcare sit with the Department of Children, Disability and Equality, which will need its own entry (it is not in my batch). The exact 2025 transfer order was not read; the split rests on the two departments' own current pages.

ETBs as a class: the youth-work function is statutory (Act s.10) and they deliver UBU with the Department, but I could not confirm from a source that ETBs hold or distribute the youth funding streams, so no 'funds' role was recorded. Worth a targeted check of an ETB youth-services page or the UBU funding guidelines in the money stage.

Leargas is not in the CSO universe (charity / company limited by guarantee) and its sponsor is the Department of Further and Higher Education, not Education. Keep it in this children's-sector list as part, or move/drop it?

gov.ie (AWS WAF), ncca.ie and examinations.ie (Cloudflare) refuse automated access, so Department pages were read through Internet Archive copies. If you want live-URL citations for those, a manual fetch in a normal browser would be needed.

Quote provenance: for Probation Service and Irish Prison Service the quotes came through WebFetch, which extracts via a model; both sites fail certificate verification when fetched directly. They were returned as exact copies but not independently re-checked. For all other bodies I read the page text directly. Do you want the Probation and IPS quotes re-gated, or set to paraphrased?

Irish Prison Service: its own About page says it deals with offenders 18 or over (verdict none), but the Department of Justice youth-justice page (last updated April 2024) says the Minister is responsible 'via the Irish Prison Service for the small number of remaining children in adult prison facilities'. Record the IPS as none on its own documents, or as part on the sponsor's statement?

Courts Service and Legal Aid Board: both administer or fund the legal process in child care proceedings, but the Courts Service does not decide cases and the Legal Aid Board's help goes to the adult who defends the application (the page says 'defend'). Are these children's functions (part) or none?

Department of Social Protection: Child Benefit, Working Family Payment and One-Parent Family Payment are paid to parents or guardians, not children; school meals reach children via schools. Counted as part. Confirm that cash payments to families count, and whether a 'payments to parents' role distinct from 'pays' is wanted.
Arts Council 'via': set to schools because Creative Schools is the child programme read, but it also has a child protection tool for arts organisations (sign-in; unread). Keep via schools?
Charities Regulator is unverified because its site returns a bot challenge to every automated request. Needs a hand check or another route; I did not bypass it.

Dormant Accounts Fund: the 2026 Action Plan table has more child/youth rows under the Departments of Children, Disability and Equality, Education and Youth and Health than are recorded here. A later stage should read the full table; should child measures there become separate rows under the delivering department?

Pobal programme list: only the first page of the programmes list (14 entries) was seen and the childcare programmes beyond AIM, CCC, Comhairle na nÓg were not read. Pobal's Data Hub 'Early Learning and Childcare Data' page was not opened, so whether Pobal publishes recipient/grant lists is unresolved.
Department of Housing: the Child and Family Homelessness Action Plan was due Q2 2026; I could not establish from pages read whether it has been published. Check before the entry is treated as final.

Sponsor names after 2025 reorganisations: Justice (now Justice, Home Affairs and Migration), Rural and Community Development (now and the Gaeltacht), Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media (now Culture, Communications and Sport) are recorded in currentSponsor from gov.ie publisher lines and one DRCD news page; the other two have no dedicated reorganisation page read.

CSO Table 4.2 (Local Authorities Non-Commercial Agencies, https://www.cso.ie/en/releasesandpublications/ep/p-rpbi/registerofpublicsectorbodies2024-final/localgovernment/) read in full: no entry has a children's body in its name. Name-only observations, not researched: 'Limerick Local Sports Partnership Ltd', 'Meath Local Sports Partnership CLG' and probably 'Sligo Sports and Recreation Partnership CLG' look like Local Sports Partnerships (covered by local-sports-partnerships); 'Fingal Community and Recreation Services CLG', 'Mulhuddart Community Centre CLG', 'Tyrrelstown Community Centre CLG', 'Athboy Social Needs and Recreational Company CLG', 'Sligo Volunteer Bureau CLG' and 'Clonmel Resource Centre CLG' are community bodies whose children role cannot be judged from the name. Childcare committees and Comhairle na nÓg are NOT rows in Table 4.2, consistent with the universe note.

Should City and County Childcare Committees be coded core? Remit is early learning/childcare programmes (children, parents, providers, childminders). I coded core because the programmes concern children; a stricter reading would be part.

Local authorities are one class entry with verdict part; per-council evidence read for only Dublin City, Cork County, Galway County and Leitrim (plus Cork City for one Comhairle sentence). Should the other councils be checked, or is class-level evidence enough?

Family homelessness (Dublin Region Homeless Executive, family hubs) is NOT established: the DRHE page read says nothing about families. It needs a page that does before any children function is recorded. Housing duties to children are also unread.

Children's library services: only Dublin City has a descriptive sentence; Cork County gave headings only and Leitrim's library page was not usable. Libraries are also a separate universe body (Local Authority Library and Archive Service, Dept of Rural and Community Development).
